title: Recap a used practice syringe with the one-handed scoop, the cap lying on its tray, the other hand kept clear
instruction: Put the pink cap that lies on the tray back onto the needle of the practice syringe, then let go.
context: Nurses (O*NET 29-1141.00), medical assistants (31-9092.00) and phlebotomists (31-9097.00), well over 500,000 US workers, sometimes cannot avoid recapping a used needle with no sharps container at hand. The safe way is the one-handed scoop: the cap lies on a surface, the needle is scooped into its mouth and pushed home, because the hand that steadies a cap is the hand that gets stuck. The cap is light and loose, the needle 1.3 mm thick, and the other hand must stay clear.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases (bases at x 0, y +-0.305), y to the robot's left, z up; table top z 0.7475. (1) Cap tray: fixed grey ABS (sRGB 0.55, 0.57, 0.60), friction 0.45/0.40, 0.5 kg: a 70 x 70 x 20 mm block (x 0.115-0.185, y -0.061 to +0.009), top at z 0.7675, with two 49 x 2 x 5 mm rails along y at x 0.1436 and 0.1564 (inner gap 10.8 mm, y -0.045 to +0.004) and a 20 x 4 x 14 mm back stop at x 0.140-0.160, y +0.006 to +0.010; plus a 20 x 70 x 20 mm rear block (y -0.109 to -0.089, same x) that carries the barrel's rear end. Between the two blocks is a 28 mm slot for the gripper pads. (2) Needle cap: translucent pink polypropylene (sRGB 0.95, 0.55, 0.70), 3 g, friction 0.35/0.30, an octagonal tube 9.6 mm across the outer flats, 1.0 mm walls, 7.6 mm across the bore flats, 49 mm bore, closed at the far end by a 1.5 mm plate; 5 mm ink ticks along its length. It lies between the rails, axis along +y, mouth centre at (0.150, -0.045, 0.7725), mouth toward the robot's right (-y), closed end 1 mm from the back stop. (3) Practice syringe: 3 mL, 6.5 g, clear polypropylene (sRGB 0.85, 0.88, 0.90), friction 0.50/0.40: barrel 9.5 mm across and 62 mm long, a 24 x 9.5 x 2 mm finger flange at its rear, a 6.6 mm luer hub 10 mm long and a steel 18 G needle (1.27 mm across, 38 mm long, flat-ground tip), 48 mm from the barrel's front shoulder to the tip. Lying needle toward +y with its front shoulder at (0.260, -0.155) and axis height 0.7723, tip at y -0.107. (4) Syringe rest: fixed grey ABS, two 20 x 40 x 20 mm blocks (y -0.219 to -0.199 and -0.171 to -0.151, x centre 0.260), each with two 6 mm lips either side of the barrel (inner gap 11 mm), leaving a 28 mm slot for the pads. (5) Zone: red tape rectangle on the table, x 0.05 to 0.36, y -0.30 to +0.03 (310 x 330 mm, taped from the arm-base midpoint with a tape measure). Fits to check: a 6.9 mm pin gauge goes the full depth into the bore and an 8.0 mm gauge does not (the bore is 7.6 mm); a 1 mm feeler gauge fits between the cap's closed end and the back stop.
scoring: Measured every control step from reset in the cap's frame (u along the bore from the mouth centre, mm): tip depth (the needle tip's u, with its lateral offset from the bore axis), shoulder gap (the barrel's front shoulder's u, 0 = at the mouth plane), axis angle between needle and bore. The holder is the arm that first closes on the barrel (opening 60 mm or less, a pad within 4 mm); the other is the off hand. Whole-run record (a linkkit History updated every control step, cleared only by the simulator reset). Gates, any time in the run, give 0: (a) a pad of the off hand over the taped zone once the holder holds; (b) a pad of either gripper within 3 mm of the cap. Ladder: 0.25 = the held needle's tip went 5 mm into the bore (lateral offset 3.5 mm or less); 0.5 = it went 30 mm in with the axis within 15 deg of the bore; 0.75 = at the end the cap is seated (tip in the bore, shoulder within 3 mm of the mouth plane and 3 mm off the axis, angle 8 deg or less); 1.0 = seated at the end, the syringe still (under 3 mm/s and 3 deg/s from its pose change between control steps) for 2 s, and the release gate: every pad point of both grippers at least 30 mm from the syringe and cap and both grippers moving under 5 mm/s for the last 1 s. Success must hold 1 s. Real trial, all by video: a top camera on the taped zone for gate (a), a side camera for gate (b) and the ticks on the translucent cap for the 5 mm and 30 mm tip depths, a ruler on the shoulder-to-mouth gap (3 mm) and a protractor on a top frame for 8 deg, a 30 mm spacer block for the release and frame differencing for stillness.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the cap between the rails, mouth toward the robot's right, with a 1 mm feeler between its closed end and the back stop. Lay the syringe in its rest, needle toward +y, flange against the rear block, shoulder at y -0.155. The tray, rest and zone tape are fixed and need no reset.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The cap is a 3 g octagonal tube (a real 18 G cap is about 1 g; 3 g is the simulator's minimum) with a straight 7.6 mm bore and no friction-fit retention: seated is judged from poses and the capped syringe rests on the tray. The needle is a rigid rod (a real one bends). The off hand cannot be stuck in simulation; gate (a) stands for the rule. Props sit on 20 mm blocks so the pads can reach under the barrel.
